font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Mortgage loans held for sale and mortgage servicing rights are carried at fair value</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">, with gains and losses from the changes</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> in fair value reflected in financial services revenue on the consolidated statements of operations.</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> Management believes carrying mortgage loans held for sale at fair value improves financial reporting by mitigating volatility in reported earnings caused by measuring the fair value of the loans and the derivative instruments used to economically hedge them. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 12pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Derivative instruments used to economically hedge our market and interest rate risk are carried at fair value. Derivative instruments typically include interest rate lock commitments and forward commitments on mortgage-backed securities. Changes in fair value of these derivatives, as well as any gains or losses upon settlement, are reflected in financial services revenue on the consolidated statements of operations. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 12pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Net gains and losses from the sale of mortgage loans held for sale are included in financial services revenue on the consolidated statements of operations, and include </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">(1)&#160;net gain on sale of loans, which </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">are recognized based upon the difference between the sales proceeds and carrying value of the related loans upon sale, with sale proceeds reflecting the cash received from investors through the sale of the mortgage loan and servicing release premium;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> (2) the fair value of originated mortgage servicing rights; (3) the change in fair value of mortgage loans held for sale; (4) the change in fair value of derivatives instruments, including </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">interest rate lock </span></p></ix:continuation></div></ix:continuation>
    <div><div class="footerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">F-</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;" class="ctHeaderFooterPage">10</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: center;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></div><hr class="pageBreak" style="margin:18pt 0pt; ct-page-break: true; page-break-after: always;"/><div class="headerContainer"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><a href="#TableOfContents" style="text-decoration: none;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; white-space:pre-wrap; color: #0000FF;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-decoration: underline;">Table of Contents</span></a></p></div></div>
    <ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-e3c9b7a1-ec62-4a3c-8e6c-d12a571d28d8-continuation-3" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-e3c9b7a1-ec62-4a3c-8e6c-d12a571d28d8-continuation-4"><div><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-d8a84039-37cb-4d6a-a09c-b939a8ebaa07-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 12pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Financial service costs on the consolidated statement of operations primarily consist of general and administrative costs to support our </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;color: #212529;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">mortgage, title, insurance brokerage and escrow services.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="ct-nonNumeric-08a82792-1c4f-442c-ab84-2bda058ac3fe" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2024_To_12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-08a82792-1c4f-442c-ab84-2bda058ac3fe-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Stock-Based Compensation </span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-08a82792-1c4f-442c-ab84-2bda058ac3fe-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We account for stock-based awards in accordance with ASC 718, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Compensation&#8212;Stock Compensation</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">.  ASC 718 requires us to estimate the grant date fair value of stock-based compensation awards and to recognize the fair value as compensation costs over the requisite service period, which is generally </span><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardAwardRequisiteServicePeriod1" id="ct-nonNumeric-fa3179ba-9a64-40e1-bcf2-1422e54a4be9" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2024_To_12_31_2024" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">three years</span></ix:nonNumeric><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">, for all awards that vest. We estimate an annual forfeiture rate at the time of grant based on historical experience, and revise the rate in subsequent periods, if necessary, based on actual forfeiture data.</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The fair value of our restricted stock units and awards in the form of unrestricted shares of common stock is equal to the closing price of our common stock on the New York Stock Exchange on the date of grant. Stock-based compensation expense associated with outstanding performance share units is measured using the grant date fair value and is based on the estimated achievement of the established performance criteria at the end of each reporting period until the performance period ends, recognized on a straight-line basis over the performance period. Stock-based compensation expense is only recognized for performance share units that we expect to vest, which we estimate based upon an assessment of the probability that the performance criteria will be achieved. The performance share units granted during the fiscal years ended December 31, 2024, 2023, and 2022 have </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; -sec-ix-hidden:ct-nonNumeric-8726d498-fbfe-4b99-9b19-4e27dd0dddb1;">three-year</span></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> performance-based metrics measured over performance periods ending on December 31 for each three-year period. </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><ix:nonNumeric name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="ct-nonNumeric-2400dd59-2ddf-4409-b3ce-827d24b50497" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2024_To_12_31_2024" escape="true" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-2400dd59-2ddf-4409-b3ce-827d24b50497-continuation-0"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Income Taxes </span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-2400dd59-2ddf-4409-b3ce-827d24b50497-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-2400dd59-2ddf-4409-b3ce-827d24b50497-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We account for income taxes in accordance with ASC 740, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Income Taxes</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">, which requires recognition of deferred tax assets and liabilities at enacted income tax rates for the temporary differences between the financial reporting bases and the tax bases of its assets and liabilities. Any effects of changes in income tax rates or tax laws are included in the provision for income taxes in the period of enactment. When it is more likely than not that a portion or all of a deferred tax asset will not be realized in the future, the Company records a corresponding valuation allowance against the deferred tax asset. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, we had </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-23cbd523-af57-45a2-8052-6fddc57627f2" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-0868ea6d-e708-425e-bdf3-74418ad8e60d" name="us-gaap:DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> valuation allowance recorded against our deferred tax assets.</span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-2400dd59-2ddf-4409-b3ce-827d24b50497-continuation-1"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In addition, when it is more likely than not that a tax position will be sustained upon examination by a tax authority that has full knowledge of all relevant information, the Company measures the amount of tax benefit from the position and records the largest amount of tax benefit that is more likely than not of being realized after settlement with a tax authority. The Company&#8217;s policy is to recognize interest to be paid on an underpayment of income taxes in interest expense and any related statutory penalties in the provision for income taxes on the consolidated statements of operations. As of December 31, 2024 and 2023 we had </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-1b1b7a8a-1765-4fef-8059-4cb246e02e66" name="us-gaap:LiabilityForUncertainTaxPositionsNoncurrent" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-8f3a516a-4746-43a1-b2d1-a72b9b6279a0" name="us-gaap:LiabilityForUncertainTaxPositionsNoncurrent" contextRef="As_Of_12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We evaluate goodwill for possible impairment in accordance with ASC 350, </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Intangibles&#8211;Goodwill and Other,</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> on an annual basis, or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be recoverable. We use a two step process to assess whether or not goodwill can be realized. The first step is a qualitative assessment that analyzes current economic indicators associated with a particular reporting unit. If the qualitative assessment indicates a stable or improved fair value, no further testing is required. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">If a qualitative assessment indicates that a significant decline to fair value of a reporting unit is more likely than not, we will proceed to the second step where we calculate the fair value of a reporting unit based on discounted future cash flows. If this step indicates that the carrying value of a reporting unit is in excess of its fair value, an impairment loss shall be recognized in an amount equal to that excess, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to that reporting unit.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-1ff782f9-7c6f-494d-836f-33efa6c58fa3" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2023_To_12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6"><ix:nonFraction id="ct-nonFraction-55496659-7615-4e95-bf57-bb3d15d98fa7" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" contextRef="Duration_1_1_2024_To_12_31_2024" unitRef="Unit1" decimals="-5" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="6">no</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">: Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2024-03&#8221;), which requires disclosure of certain costs and expenses on an interim and annual basis in the notes to the financial statements. ASU 2024-03 will become effective for us for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2027. Early adoption is permitted, and guidance should be applied prospectively, with an option to apply guidance retrospectively. We are currently evaluating the impact of the adoption of ASU 2024-03 on our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU No. 2023-09, &#8220;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Income Taxes (Topic 740)</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">: Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2023-09&#8221;). ASU 2023-09 requires more disaggregated income tax disclosures, including additional information in the rate reconciliation and additional disclosures about income taxes paid. ASU 2023-09 will become effective for us for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2025. Early adoption is permitted, and guidance should be applied prospectively, with an option to apply guidance retrospectively. We are currently evaluating the impact of the adoption of ASU 2023-09 on our consolidated financial statements and related disclosures.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">In November 2023, the FASB issued ASU No. 2023-07, &#8220;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Segment Reporting (Topic 280)</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">: Improvements to Reportable Segment Disclosures&#8221; (&#8220;ASU 2023-07&#8221;). ASU 2023-07 requires disclosure of significant segment expenses that are regularly provided to the chief operating decision maker (&#8220;CODM&#8221;) and included within each reported measure of segment profit or loss. The guidance also expands disclosure requirements for interim periods, as well as requires disclosure of other segment items, including the title and position of the entity&#8217;s CODM. ASU 2023-07 became effective for us for the fiscal year ending December 31, 2024 and we </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; background: #FFFFFF;color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">applied the amendments retrospectively to all prior periods presented in our consolidated financial statements. </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">See </span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Note 2 &#8211; Reporting Segments in the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></p></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-e3c9b7a1-ec62-4a3c-8e6c-d12a571d28d8-continuation-5"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></ix:continuation></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; color: #000000;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></div>

Our Century Communities brand is managed by geographic location, and each of our four geographic regions offers a wide range of buyer profiles including: entry-level, first and second time move-up, and lifestyle homebuyers, and provides our homebuyers with the ability to personalize their homes through certain option and upgrade selections. For all of the segments, the CODMs use segment income before income tax expense in the annual budget and forecasting process. The CODMs consider budget-to-actual forecast variances for income before tax expense on a monthly basis for evaluating performance of each segment and making decisions about allocating capital and other resources to each segment. The measure of segment assets is reported on the consolidated balance sheets as total assets. Self-Insurance Reserve</span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-316863f7-904e-4978-875e-a5d6bd6522ea-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span id="_Hlk186724726" style="text-decoration: none;"></span><span id="_Hlk155258027" style="text-decoration: none;"></span><span id="_Hlk123125906" style="text-decoration: none;"></span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We maintain general liability insurance coverage, including coverage for certain construction defects after homes have been delivered and premise operations during construction. These insurance policies are designed to protect us against a portion of the risk of loss from claims, subject to certain self-insured per occurrence and aggregate retentions, deductibles, and available policy limits. In circumstances where we have elected to retain a higher portion of the overall risk for construction defect claims in return for a lower initial premium, we reserve for the estimated self-insured retention costs that we will incur that are above our coverage limits or that are not covered by our insurance policies. The reserve is recorded on an undiscounted basis at the time revenue is recognized for each home closing. Amounts accrued, which are included in accrued expenses and other liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets, are based on third party actuarial analyses that are primarily based upon industry data and partially on our historical claims, which include estimates of claims incurred but not yet reported. Adjustments to estimated reserves are recorded in the period in which the change in estimate occurs. Our self-insurance liability is presented on a gross basis without consideration of insurance recoveries and amounts we have paid on behalf of and expect to recover from other parties, if any. Estimates of insurance recoveries and amounts we have paid on behalf of and expect to recover from other parties, if any, are recorded as receivables when such recoveries are considered probable. Fair Value Disclosures </span></ix:nonNumeric></p><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-c44b59b5-fbcf-49f2-8c68-f83a5db1c055-continuation-0" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-c44b59b5-fbcf-49f2-8c68-f83a5db1c055-continuation-1"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Fair value measurements are used for the Company&#8217;s mortgage loans held for sale, mortgage loans held for investment, mortgage servicing rights, interest rate lock commitments and other derivative instruments on a recurring basis.  We also utilize fair value measurements on a non-recurring basis for inventories, and intangible assets when events and circumstances indicate that the carrying value is not recoverable. The fair value hierarchy and its application to the Company&#8217;s assets and liabilities is as follows:</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 12pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Level&#160;1 &#8211; Quoted prices for identical instruments in active markets. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Level&#160;2 &#8211; Quoted prices for similar instruments in active markets; quoted prices for identical or similar instruments in markets that are inactive; and model-derived valuations in which all significant inputs and significant value drivers are observable in active markets at the measurement date. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 0;margin-left: 0.50in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.250in;">&#61623;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Mortgage loans held for sale</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> &#8211; Fair value is based on quoted market prices for committed and uncommitted mortgage loans.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0.50in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.250in;">&#61623;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Derivative assets and liabilities</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> &#8211; Derivative assets are associated with interest rate lock commitments and investor commitments on loans and may also be associated with forward mortgage-backed securities contracts. Derivative liabilities are associated with forward mortgage-backed securities contracts. Fair value is based on market prices for similar instruments.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Level&#160;3 &#8211; Valuations derived from techniques where one or more significant inputs or significant value drivers are unobservable in active markets at the measurement date. </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0.50in;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;text-indent: -0.25in;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; display: inline-block;font-family: Symbol;font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;text-indent: 0;width: 0.250in;">&#61623;</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: italic;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Mortgage servicing rights</span><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> &#8211; The fair value of the mortgage servicing rights is calculated using third-party valuations. The key assumptions, which are generally unobservable inputs, used in the valuation of the mortgage servicing rights include mortgage prepayment rates, discount rates and cost to service.</span><span id="_Hlk94108307" style="text-decoration: none;"></span></p></ix:continuation></div>

    <div><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-6fd540ab-707a-444d-b3f7-fdc9bb2eda81-continuation-1" continuedAt="ct-nonNumeric-6fd540ab-707a-444d-b3f7-fdc9bb2eda81-continuation-2"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-3c7e94da-f1ad-4a33-b5d9-676a60a20560-continuation-0"><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: .001pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 0;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 12pt;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: bold;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Legal Proceedings </span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 12pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 5pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">The Company and our subsidiaries and affiliates are subject to claims, lawsuits and other legal actions from time to time that arise primarily in the ordinary course of business, which consist mostly of construction claims, but also could include warranty, workers&#8217; compensation, tort, breach of contract, employment, personal injury, and other similar claims.  It is the opinion of management that if the construction or warranty claims have merit, parties other than the Company would be, at least in part, liable for the claims, and eventual outcome of these claims will not have a material adverse effect upon our consolidated financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.  When we believe that a loss is probable and estimable, we record the estimated amount to other accrued liabilities included in accrued expenses and other liabilities on the consolidated balance sheet.</span></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 5pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 5pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">Under various insurance policies, we have the ability to recoup costs in excess of applicable self-insured retentions.  Estimates of such amounts are recorded in accounts receivable on our consolidated balance sheet when recovery is probable. </span></p></ix:continuation><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 5pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 5pt;text-align: justify;"><ix:continuation id="ct-nonNumeric-6fd540ab-707a-444d-b3f7-fdc9bb2eda81-continuation-2"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;">We do not believe that the ultimate resolution of any claims, lawsuits and other legal actions will have a material adverse effect upon our consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</span></ix:continuation></p><p dir="ltr" style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', 'serif';font-size: 10pt;line-height: 108%;margin-bottom: 5pt;margin-left: 0;margin-right: 0;margin-top: 5pt;text-align: justify;"><span style="white-space:pre-wrap; font-size: 10pt;font-style: normal;font-weight: normal;margin: 0;padding: 0;"> </span></p></div>
